summary: The script is generally defensive: it excludes empty normalized names from exact agreement, asserts merge coverage, and explicitly distinguishes agreement from accuracy. The remaining numerical concern is that “Ours+Anc” uses a fallback rule that is neither the linkage pipeline’s raw-empty rule nor the scoring code’s normalized-empty definition, so it can silently score the wrong source on unusual model strings.

findings.title: “Ours+Anc” applies an inconsistent definition of an empty model field
findings.what_the_code_does: The fallback indicators use `strtrim(namefrst_ml)==""` and `strtrim(namelast_ml_ditto)==""` before normalization. Scoring later applies `pnorm`, under which nonblank values containing only punctuation, annotations, or removable titles can become empty and score zero, while the report describes Ancestry as filling an empty model field. Conversely, whitespace-only values trigger fallback here although the cited linkage construction tests raw `==""`.
findings.why_it_matters: If either kind of value exists, reported Ours+Anc agreement and Jaro-Winkler means use a different transcription source than the prose and linkage comparison imply. The numerical size cannot be established without the data.
findings.how_to_check: After constructing normalized model fields, run counts for `(strtrim(namefrst_ml)!="" & cf_ml=="")`, `(strtrim(namelast_ml_ditto)!="" & cl_ml=="")`, and raw-nonempty whitespace-only fields. Recompute Ours+Anc using raw-empty, trimmed-empty, and normalized-empty fallback rules and compare the table means.
findings.suggested_fix: Choose the intended definition explicitly. To reproduce the linkage pipeline, use raw `==""`; to mean analytically usable names, normalize first and fall back when the normalized value is empty. Update the report text to name the chosen rule.

verified_clean.item: Exact agreement cannot be inflated by empty-string equality
verified_clean.evidence: Both the full-name and first-name indicators require nonempty normalized source values at MATCHING/profile_names_jw.do:132-133.

verified_clean.item: Empty normalized source names receive zero Jaro-Winkler similarity
verified_clean.evidence: `jwpair` excludes empty pairs from calculation, asserts scores for nonempty pairs, and assigns zero where the candidate is empty at MATCHING/profile_names_jw.do:71-81.

verified_clean.item: The distinct-pair similarity merge has a unique using-side key
verified_clean.evidence: The helper retains only the two name fields and executes `duplicates drop` before `merge m:1` at MATCHING/profile_names_jw.do:72-79.

verified_clean.item: The reference-name merge rejects unmatched observations
Sex-specific reference-name requirements match the reported measures
verified_clean.evidence: Men require nonempty profile first and last names, while women require only a profile first name, at MATCHING/profile_names_jw.do:92-98.

verified_clean.item: The model-name-present restriction uses normalized names and the correct sex-specific fields
verified_clean.evidence: Normalized model first-name and surname availability are captured at MATCHING/profile_names_jw.do:135-139; `hasml` requires both for men and only first name for women at MATCHING/profile_names_jw.do:148-155.

verified_clean.item: Women are excluded from surname and full-name summaries
verified_clean.evidence: Surname candidates and scores are suppressed for non-men at MATCHING/profile_names_jw.do:140-145, and women's output measures are limited to exact-first and JW-first at MATCHING/profile_names_jw.do:207-210.

verified_clean.item: The ditto-resolved surname is accurately disclosed
verified_clean.evidence: The computation uses `namelast_ml_ditto` at MATCHING/profile_names_jw.do:123-124, and the emitted prose identifies it as a surname with ditto marks resolved at MATCHING/profile_names_jw.do:197.

verified_clean.item: The generated prose does not equate agreement with accuracy
verified_clean.evidence: The output explicitly says `Agreement with a selected, FamilySearch-linked reference, not accuracy` at MATCHING/profile_names_jw.do:197.

verified_clean.item: Full-name similarity matches its documented equal-weight definition
verified_clean.evidence: The code computes `(jf_... + jl_...)/2` at MATCHING/profile_names_jw.do:144, matching the definition at MATCHING/profile_names_jw.do:15-19.

verified_clean.item: Core sample sizes and exact-agreement benchmarks are checked before output
verified_clean.evidence: Male and female sample counts are asserted and twelve sets of rounded agreement rates are checked at MATCHING/profile_names_jw.do:157-191.

review_limits: No paper draft was supplied, so claims-vs-code review was limited to claims embedded in the target's comments and generated-report text.
The external census and profile datasets were unavailable, and the Stata pipeline could not be run; the prevalence and numerical effect of inconsistent empty-field definitions could not be measured.
The installed version and runtime behavior of the external SSC `jarowinkler` command could not be independently verified.

The checked-in MATCHING/results/profile_names_jw.md predates the current target: it lacks the two model-name-present sections added at MATCHING/profile_names_jw.do:199. Consequently, those new output values could not be inspected.
